title: Reference rhythm: dotted cell and whole-bar alternatives
playback_note: Three versions of the same generated riff with matched offline alphaTab 1.8.4 GM guitar, tempo and gain. The two alternatives edit different places: the dotted cell changes bars 6 and 14; the whole-bar cell changes bar 10. The first bar is a pickup. Source written ties are resolved into exact holds, not reproduced as original notation. Musical preference is still for you to judge.
questions: Does the dotted cell fit the melodic arrivals in bars 6 and 14?
Does the whole-bar alternative leave useful space in bar 10?
Which version would you keep developing?

versions.label: Original generated riff
versions.description: Untouched generated current state, before timing transfer.

versions.label: Dotted cell and return
versions.description: Complete two-quarter-note cell: a dotted eighth, a held middle note and a final sixteenth. Both linked occurrences change together in bars 6 and 14. Four attacks and four written holds change; all pitches, contacts and articulations stay fixed.

versions.label: Complete-bar alternative
versions.description: Complete observed four-attack 4/4 bar in bar 10, with a longer first note and two eighth rests. One attack and four written holds change. The actual score barlines account for the pickup; all pitches, contacts and articulations stay fixed.
